focus: Section 3.2.1, Scaled Dot-Product Attention. Explain scaled dot-product attention using small, editable Q, K, and V matrices. Show similarity scores, normalized attention weights, and the output. Let the learner edit values and switch scaling on/off. Guide them through equal scores and a dominant score. Check that each row of weights sums to one and that the output equals the weighted sum of V. Do not train a Transformer.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows matrix multiplication and basic probability but has not studied Transformers.

plan.concept: Scaled dot-product attention: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V, with editable Q, K, V and a scaling toggle.
learning_outcomes: Compute similarity scores QK^T and see how dividing by sqrt(d_k) changes them.
Convert scores to attention weights with softmax and verify each row sums to 1.
See the output as a weighted average of the value rows.
Explain why scaling matters when d_k is large.
plan.visual_strategy: Pipeline of score -> scaled score -> weights -> output, plus heatmaps of scores and weights, a table of the output rows, and a sweep showing how the largest weight grows with d_k when scaling is off.
plan.misconception: Softmax weights are not a similarity ranking alone: they are a probability distribution over value rows, and without scaling large d_k makes that distribution nearly one-hot.
